issues.legal_issue: A court retains jurisdiction to extend the time for compliance with a conditional decree for specific performance until the sale deed is executed.
material_facts: A decree for specific performance required the respondent to pay specified sums within three months and, in default, to execute the sale deed.
The sale deed had not been executed when the respondent applied for rescission and an extension of time.
issues.conclusion: The court retained jurisdiction to deal with the decree and had discretion to extend the time for compliance.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28(1) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 permits an application to rescind a specific-performance contract when the required payment is not made within the time allowed. That power shows the court does not become functus officio upon making the decree; until the sale deed is executed, it retains jurisdiction, including power to extend the time for compliance. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.specific_performance_decree_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a decree for specific performance of a contract involving immovable property.
predicates.conditional_payment_required: The decree requires a party to make a payment as a condition of compliance.
predicates.sale_deed_unexecuted: The sale deed required by the decree has not yet been executed.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance proceeding involves conditional payment and the sale deed remains unexecuted, the court retains power to extend the time for compliance.

issues.legal_issue: An application to extend the time for compliance with a specific-performance decree does not require an explanation for every day of delay as an application to condone delay under limitation law would.
material_facts: The respondent applied for rescission and extension after a delay of about seven and a half years.
The execution court found no satisfactory explanation for the delay, but exercised discretion to extend the time for compliance.
The High Court upheld the extension and directed additional compensation.
issues.conclusion: The absence of a satisfactory explanation for every day of delay did not prevent the courts from exercising their discretion to extend time; the extension was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28(1) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 permits the court to extend the time for compliance with a specific-performance decree. An application for extension of time is not an application for condonation of delay under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, and need not explain every day of delay. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.specific_performance_execution_proceedin: The proceeding concerns enforcement of a decree for specific performance.
predicates.extension_of_compliance_time_sought: A party bound by the decree asks the court for more time to comply with it.
predicates.court_exercised_extension_discretion: The court exercises its discretion to grant more time for compliance.

issues.definition: In enforcement of a specific-performance decree, when more time is sought and the court exercises its discretion to grant it, the extension is upheld without requiring the application to meet the standard for condoning limitation delay.

issues.legal_issue: Additional compensation for loss from delayed payment may be upheld when it accords with the parties’ contractual provision for damages.
material_facts: The contract quantified damages for non-performance at Rs. 2,000.
The High Court directed an additional payment of Rs. 16,000 to compensate for the loss of enjoyment of money, calculated by reference to the contractual damages over eight years.
The Supreme Court upheld that additional payment as being in terms of the contract.
issues.conclusion: The additional compensation directed by the High Court was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The court upheld the additional compensation because the parties had quantified damages in the contract and the amount was given in terms of that contractual provision. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this ruling.

predicates.specific_performance_execution_proceedin: The proceeding concerns enforcement of a decree for specific performance.
predicates.contract_quantifies_damages_for_nonperfo: The parties’ contract states a measure of damages for non-performance.
predicates.additional_compensation_tracks_contractu: The court awards additional compensation by reference to the measure of damages stated in the contract.

issues.definition: In enforcement of a specific-performance decree, additional compensation is upheld when the contract provides a measure of damages for non-performance and the award follows that measure.
